findings.title: Device limit bypassed: cache entry set before the limit check fails
findings.body: `tagDeviceUI` writes the device key to `localCache` before calling `CreateOrUpdateDevice`. When the limit is reached, the first request from a new device gets `ErrDeviceLimitReached` and authentication is rejected, but the cache entry stays. For the next 29 minutes every request from that device hits the cache, `TagDevice` returns nil, and the client authenticates successfully. The limit only blocks one request per device per cache window. Set the cache entry only after the store call succeeds, or don't cache when the error is `ErrDeviceLimitReached`.

findings.title: Count-then-insert is not atomic, so the limit can be exceeded
findings.body: `CreateOrUpdateDevice` runs `CountDevices` and then does a separate INSERT, with no transaction or lock around them. Concurrent first requests from different new devices can all see `count < deviceLimit` and all insert. The configured limit is therefore not enforced under concurrent load, including across multiple Grafana instances.

findings.title: rowsAffected==0 wrongly reports limit reached for existing devices on MySQL
findings.body: Once the limit is reached, `updateDevice` returns `ErrDeviceLimitReached` whenever the UPDATE affects 0 rows. By default MySQL reports affected rows as changed rows, not matched rows. If an already-registered device is updated with the same IP and user agent within the same second (DATETIME has second precision), nothing changes and 0 is returned. That legitimate device is then denied anonymous access. Check existence with a SELECT, or treat matched rows as success.

findings.title: ProvideAnonDBStore now takes a bare int64, which breaks wire injection
findings.body: `ProvideAnonDBStore` now requires an `int64` argument, and `ProvideAnonymousDeviceService` no longer consumes `AnonStore`. If the wire provider sets still list `anonstore.ProvideAnonDBStore` and bind `AnonStore`, wire generation fails because nothing provides `int64`. No wire.go changes are part of this PR. Remove the provider from the wire sets, or have it take `*setting.Cfg`.

findings.title: Device tagging moved from async to the synchronous auth path
findings.body: `TagDevice` used to run in a background goroutine with a timeout. It now runs inline in `Authenticate`. On every cache miss, the anonymous request now waits for DB writes, plus a full COUNT over `anon_device` when a limit is configured. This happens even when `device_limit` is 0 and enforcement isn't needed. Slow or locked DBs now directly add latency to, or stall, anonymous page loads.

findings.title: Limit test doesn't verify existing devices still work at the limit
findings.body: `TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit` only checks that a new device is rejected. It never checks that the already-registered device can still be updated once the limit is reached, which is the core path through `updateDevice`. It also has no service-level test that rejection persists across repeated requests, which would have caught the cache bypass.

findings.title: New `device_limit` setting is undocumented
findings.body: `[auth.anonymous] device_limit` is read here, but it is not added to conf/defaults.ini, conf/sample.ini, or the docs. Operators have no way to discover the option, or to learn that 0 means unlimited.
